text.tspan: On the LAN: NDP (ICMPv6, multicast) replaces ARP; SLAAC builds the address
3 · SLAAC: the host builds its address
DAD: is anyone already using it?
tell me your MAC (= ARP request)
here is my MAC (= ARP reply)
The MAC shows in every address, so the device can be
tracked. Modern OSes use random interface IDs.
NDP, router discovery, duplicate address detection
and path MTU discovery ("packet too big", type 2)
all run on it. RFC 4890 lists what to allow.
